Given a generalized Dicke state (GDS) of $(j-1)$ quantum registers, each assigned to a particle, the algorithm produces another GDS of $j$ registers (of $n_{qb}$ qubits each) using a mere $\mathcal{O}(j\log_2^2 j + j n_{qb})$ $\mathtt{CNOT}$ and single-qubit gates, and $3j+\lceil\log_2j\rceil+\mathcal{O}(\max(n_{qb},\log_2 j))$ clean auxiliary qubits. The (anti)symmetrizing operator constructed for this purpose depends on the quantum numbers of the additional particle being introduced or ``created''. The algorithm improves upon the construction presented in Appendix A of \cite{Galvez-Viruet:2024hry} by almost two powers of $j$ and is on par with the most efficient methods to date, while ideally suited for dynamical memory management with variable particle number. We exemplify its applicability with a small selection of problems from hadron physics which are expected to be addressable with upcoming quantum computers.

title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $φ^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
abstract: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in $φ^4$ theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.

title: BFKL as a matrix: anomalous dimensions and running-coupling
abstract: The BFKL equation resums high-energy logarithms in a scattering process. We average over the angle between transverse momenta and replace the squared transverse momentum (virtuality) by $D$ discrete cells. The evolution equation becomes a real symmetric $D \times D$ matrix $H_D$. Its off-diagonal entries describe real gluon emissions that move the scale from one cell to another. Its diagonal is the virtual correction that makes those emissions finite. Powers of the matrix build up ordered emission histories, the inverse matrix propagates the amplitude between scales, and the eigenvalues and eigenvectors give the positions and the strengths of the singularities that control growth with rapidity. A row far from both ends of the matrix reproduces the BFKL eigenvalue. Some regions bring corrections to this for a finite Hamiltonian. These are the missing regions below the first cell and above the last cell, and the cell width. Matching the two scale powers allowed by a row yields the anomalous dimension. The matrix reproduces the leading-logarithmic small-$x$ coefficients. At fixed coupling, every finite matrix has only isolated poles. We show that they become increasingly dense as the logarithmic virtuality range grows, with a condition on their residues needed for the sum to approach the continuous BFKL Regge cut. Multiplying each real emission by a Bessel factor, which sums the leading double logarithms of the scale ratio, provides a test of how the fixed-coupling spectrum and its leading eigenvectors respond when long jumps in scale are suppressed. Finally, we place a running coupling which avoids the Landau pole. The number of positive low-scale states grows linearly with the logarithmic length, with a slope fixed by the kernel. A one-loop coupling with Landau pole, combined with a lower wall, creates an ultraviolet turning point and an Airy decay region.

title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
abstract: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform-mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW. Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2σ$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.

title: RG evolution of the $B$-meson LCDA and radiative jet function at three loops
abstract: We calculate the three-loop evolution kernel of the light-cone distribution amplitude of the $B$ meson, together with the radiative jet function in the leptonic radiative decay $B^-\toγ\ell^-\barν$ for the first time. Representing the light-cone distribution amplitude as the discontinuity of a matrix element containing an inverse differential operator, we compute the partonic matrix element in momentum space with a novel method of infrared subtraction. We show that its infrared singularities are governed by the same anomalous dimension as that of the heavy-light quark form factor, so that they can be subtracted without introducing any infrared regulator, thereby preserving gauge invariance and avoiding additional complexity in the Feynman integrals. Based on the renormalization-group invariance of the factorization theorem, we derive the renormalization factor of the radiative jet function, and confirm that it removes all divergences of the bare three-loop radiative jet function. Our results enable the resummation of large logarithms in exclusive $B$ decays at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy.

title: Regionally Optimal Contour Deformations with Neural Networks
abstract: In this article, we explore the use of contour deformation for the numerical evaluation of Feynman integrals after sector decomposition. In existing codes, the contour of integration is determined heuristically for each phase-space point by sampling the integrand. In this work, we introduce a method for choosing the contour deformation for an entire phase-space region using only an initial sampling or training step. We demonstrate that the resulting integrand has a lower variance than that obtained with heuristic methods and show that optimising a contour to reduce the estimated error of a Quasi-Monte Carlo sample is an ill-defined problem. The a priori knowledge of the integration path obtained in this work can be used to improve the speed of conventional integration methods or be leveraged for integration using neural networks, where, crucially, it removes the need to retrain the neural network for each phase-space point. The techniques described in this work can be adapted to other problems where a non-trivial integration path has to be chosen subject to a set of constraints.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sequence Models for Sample-Efficient Energy Regression in Simulated Calorimeter Showers
abstract: Energy reconstruction from electromagnetic calorimeter data underpins particle identification, event reconstruction and precision measurements in high-energy physics. Machine learning already performs well on this task, yet two questions remain open: how much the choice of data representation matters, and whether hybrid quantum-classical models add value in practice. We compare classical and quantum-enhanced models for incident positron energy reconstruction on the CaloGAN dataset, a public benchmark of 100,000 simulated electromagnetic shower events spanning 1 to 100 GeV. Eight architectures, namely SVR, ANN, CNN and LSTM together with their quantum counterparts, are trained on three calorimeter representations: engineered physical features, calorimeter images, and longitudinal shower sequences. Models that follow the longitudinal development of the shower reach the highest accuracy, which points to the value of physically informed representations. The hybrid QLSTM gives the lowest reconstruction error, with an RMSE of 0.294 GeV. Under matched-data conditions with only 1,500 training events, the QLSTM improves on the classical LSTM by 52.7% and also surpasses an LSTM trained on the full set. These observations indicate that longitudinal representations are central to calorimeter energy reconstruction and give preliminary evidence that hybrid quantum-classical sequence models can be more sample-efficient for regression in high-energy physics.

title: Gravitational form factors of $ρ$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD
abstract: We compute the gravitational form factors and mechanical properties of the $ρ$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD, a holographic model of QCD with backreacting flavor and dynamical chiral symmetry breaking. The parameters of the model are taken from an earlier fit to meson spectra and are not adjusted to form factor data. Both mesons are described by a single spin-1 field, and the six form factors are identified from the matrix element of the energy-momentum tensor with two spin-1 states, following the holographic dictionary. We find that $A_0 = J$ and $A_1 = 0$ hold identically in the model, and show that the remaining form factors $E$, $D_0$ and $D_1$ are regular at zero momentum transfer. We compare the form factors of $ρ$ with results from the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, a light-cone constituent quark model and the hard-wall holographic model. From the form factors, we compute the monopole and quadrupole distributions of energy, pressure and shear force in the Breit frame. The D-term, defined for spin-1 hadrons as the forward value of the combination $\mathcal{D}_0(t)$ of form factors, is found to be $-2.98$ for the $ρ$ and $-7.43$ for the $a_1$ meson. The mass and mechanical radii are $0.81$~fm and $0.89$~fm for $ρ$, and $0.73$~fm and $0.80$~fm for $a_1$.

title: Complementary Approach to Anisotropic Flows in Heavy-Ion Collisions
abstract: We present a complementary count of directed flow \(v_1\) and elliptic flow \(v_2\). It does not replace known methods. A fixed laboratory plane defines up--down and left--right asymmetries. A scan of the test angle is written down as a theoretical proposal. Each event is given one angle \(α\) drawn uniformly on \([0,2π)\), the fixed plane is rotated by \(α\), and the asymmetries are averaged over events. With \(θ=α\) known, the linear fit recovers \(v_n^{\mathrm{true}}\). The quadratic mean, Eq.~(5), agrees with the pair form, Eq.~(21), in which the \(1/N\) self term cancels, and both sit above \(v_n^{\mathrm{true}}\) because the event noise in \(A\) is squared. The time for one count grows linearly with the number of particles. The pair sum, and the usual two-particle correlation, grow as the square of that number. The sample is PHSD Au+Au at \(\sqrt{s_{NN}}=9.2\,\mathrm{GeV}\), \(b=4.0\)--\(5.2\,\mathrm{fm}\).

title: Connecting High-Twist Expansion and Color Glass Condensate Dynamics
abstract: The high-twist (HT) expansion and the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) describe nuclear multiple scattering in complementary kinematic regimes. For direct-photon production in proton-nucleus collisions, we formulate an arbitrary-order multiple-scattering master expression that includes photon emission before, between, or after the ordered quark scatterings in the amplitude and its conjugate. In the high-energy limit, resumming multiple scatterings to all orders recovers the CGC Wilson-line dipole result. However, the naive power expansion of the eikonal CGC result reproduces the leading twist but only part of the twist-four contribution obtained in the HT expansion. Including longitudinal sub-eikonal phases and Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal interference restores the CGC-HT correspondence through twist-4.

title: Why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
abstract: Since a strong magnetic field is generated in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, novel phenomena have been predicted to occur in the quark-gluon plasma produced in these collisions. However, these predictions have not yet been convincingly confirmed experimentally. We reanalyze the generation and evolution of the magnetic field which plays a key role in the phenomena. Using the method of one-sided Fourier transformation, we reconcile the description in frequency and wave-vector space, which is required to properly account for the electromagnetic properties of the quark-gluon plasma, with the initial-value nature of the problem arising from the creation of the plasma medium at the moment of collision. We show that the currents induced in the quark-gluon plasma, which sustain the magnetic field, develop with a delay and are consequently less effective than usually assumed. Moreover, because the plasma initially consists predominantly of electrically neutral gluons, while charged quarks emerge at a later stage, the induced currents are further delayed. Consequently, a magnitude of the field present in the quark-gluon plasma is significantly lower than earlier estimates suggested. This may explain why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
